summary: An above-grade wastewater pump station at 455 Berry Street between 6th and 7th Streets, constructed in 1979 and upgraded in 2010, with a capacity of 103 million gallons per day, which SF Planning's 2020 sea level rise assessment describes as operating continuously in dry and wet weather and conveying flows to the Southeast Treatment Plant.

facts.value: 455 Berry St, near Mission Bay between 6th and 7th Streets
San Francisco Public Utilities Commission Wastewater Enterprise manages the city's wastewater assets (chapter-level statement, not specific to this station)
Serves the Channel and Northshore drainage basins; conveys wastewater through the Channel force main to the Southeast Treatment Plant

sources.title: Sea Level Rise Vulnerability and Consequences Assessment, Chapter 7 Wastewater (Photo 7.1 and section 7.1.1.1)

open_questions: No source read records the construction of the 1979 station beyond the year, or what the 2010 upgrade involved.
The report is dated by its PDF metadata (February 2020); it is the only source read, so the station's current operating state is as described in 2020.
Whether the station sits inside the Mission Bay redevelopment area boundary was not re-checked here; the map note places it in Mission Bay South.
